Report_ID: Cumulative 16-week complete response (16w-CR) rate — all patients
Title: Metformin plus Megestrol Acetate (MA) compared with MA alone as well differentiated endometrial cancer: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Yang, Gulinazi, Du, et al.
Comment: Per-arm event counts are not stated as totals in the text; they were summed from Table 1's separately reported histology strata (AEH 21/53 and EEC 2/14 for MA+metformin = 23/67, 34.3%; AEH 10/49 and EEC 2/9 for MA-only = 12/58, 20.7%), consistent with the verbatim percentages and the stated analysed n=125. Randomised Ns were 76 (MA+metformin) and 74 (MA-only).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('MA + metformin (megestrol acetate 160 mg/day plus metformin 500 mg three times daily)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Women aged 18-45 with primary atypical endometrial hyperplasia or well-differentiated endometrioid endometrial cancer desiring fertility preservation
Recruitment source: Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai
Outcome measurement: Number of women achieving complete response (return to normal endometrium) out of patients analysed within 16 weeks (intention-to-treat, n=125)
Outcome variable: Cumulative 16-week complete response (16w-CR) rate — all patients
additional_group_ns: Randomised: MA+metformin n=76 (61 AEH, 15 EEC); MA-only n=74 (62 AEH, 12 EEC). No third arm.

Author: Tehranian et al.
Comment: Text reports P = 0.02 while Table 2 footnote reports p = 0.028 for the biopsy-findings distribution; 60 were randomised (30 per arm) but 56 analysed (29 vs 27) - analysed Ns used per extraction rules. Report_ID: Complete response (complete histological regression of EAH to proliferative or secretory endometrium) at 12 weeks
Title: Conservative therapy with metformin plus megestrol acetate for endometrial atypical hyperplasia
Author: Shan W, Wang C, Zhang Z, Gu C, Ning C, Luo X, Zhou Q, Chen X
Comment: The reported p=0.105 is from a two-sample Mann-Whitney comparison of the overall response distribution (CR/PR/NR), not a 2x2 test of CR alone. Counts 6/8 and 2/8 are explicitly reported. Study described as prospective pilot study with randomization; 16 of 30 enrolled patients analysed.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('MET group (megestrol acetate 160 mg/day + metformin 0.5 g thrice daily)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Women aged <=45 years with endometrial atypical hyperplasia desiring fertility preservation and meeting at least one metabolic syndrome criterion
Recruitment source: Outpatients of the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai
Outcome measurement: Number of women with complete response (CR) out of number analysed per arm
Outcome variable: Complete response (complete histological regression of EAH to proliferative or secretory endometrium) at 12 weeks

Report_ID: Complete histological regression (treatment response) of endometrial hyperplasia/proliferative disorder at end of 3-month treatment
Title: The Comparative Effect of Combination of Metformin and Megestrol Acetate With Megestrol Acetate Alone on Endometrial Growth Disorders
Author: Sayyah-Melli et al.
Comment: Events (responders) derived by subtracting the paper's explicitly reported non-responder counts from the arm denominators implied by the reported percentages (3/43 = 7%; 2/41 = 4.9%). The paper elsewhere states 44 and 40 completed per arm, so denominators are slightly inconsistent; 43 and 41 were used as they reproduce the stated percentages and sum to the 84 analysed participants.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Metformin 500 mg BID + megestrol acetate 40 mg/d (Group 1)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: women with abnormal uterine bleeding and disordered proliferative or hyperplastic endometrium with or without atypia
Recruitment source: Alzahra Teaching Hospital, Tabriz University of Medical Sciences
Outcome measurement: Number of women responding to treatment on endometrial pathology (events = responders; derived from reported non-response 3 (7%) vs 2 (4.9%))
Outcome variable: Complete histological regression (treatment response) of endometrial hyperplasia/proliferative disorder at end of 3-month treatment
